text:
alex: Hi all, I'm Alex (started today). On WSL2 (Ubuntu). Followed the onboarding steps for kubeconfig but `kubectl get pods -n redwood-dev` gives `Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "system:anonymous"` — I expected my SSO identity. Any idea?

devon: hey alex, welcome! Did you run `aws sso login` in your WSL shell (not powershell)? Sometimes people run it in Windows and the creds don't show up in WSL. Also check `kubectl config view --raw --minify` to see which user entry is active.

alex: I did SSO from Windows Powershell earlier. Running `aws sso login --profile redwood-sso` inside WSL gave me the browser popup; after that `aws sts get-caller-identity --profile redwood-sso` shows my account. But kubectl still returns Forbidden.

pri: check `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl config view --raw` — maybe your kubeconfig merged with a context that uses a tokenless user. Also run `KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config kubectl auth can-i list pods -n redwood-dev --as=system:serviceaccount:redwood:ci-bot` just to test, but you likely won't have permissions.

devon: another common gotcha on WSL: environment variables for `KUBECONFIG` or `AWS_PROFILE` set in Windows don't automatically propagate. Confirm `echo $KUBECONFIG` and `echo $AWS_PROFILE` inside WSL.

alex: `echo $KUBECONFIG` is empty. I do have `~/.kube/config` in WSL. `kubectl config current-context` prints `redwood-dev`. `kubectl config view --raw` shows a user entry with `exec` calling `aws` and args `eks get-token`. The exec output printed `token: null` when I ran it by hand: `aws eks get-token --cluster-name redwood-dev --region us-west-2 --profile redwood-sso` returns a JSON with an expiry and token normally; mine printed a token field but I guess kubectl didn't pick it up.

eng-infra: @alex can you paste the exact error from `kubectl` when you append `-v=8` to the command? `kubectl get pods -n redwood-dev -v=8` will show the exec plugin output. Also run `which aws` to ensure the `aws` binary in WSL is the CLI v2.

alex: pasted snippet: "exec plugin produced no auth data" and in the logs the aws command exited 0 and printed `{"kind":"ExecCredential","apiVersion":"client.authentication.k8s.io/v1beta1","status":{"token":null}}`. So `aws eks get-token` is returning status.token as null. When I run it without WSL (powershell) it returns a token.

pri: that means your SSO session in WSL isn't linked. Try removing cached SSO files under `~/.aws/sso/cache` in WSL and re-run `aws sso login --profile redwood-sso` within WSL. If your browser opens in Windows, complete the login and then confirm `~/.aws/sso/cache` has a json file.

devon: also check time sync in WSL (`date`) — if the clock is off it can cause the token to be treated as expired.

alex: deleted cache, re-logged in inside WSL, `aws eks get-token --cluster-name redwood-dev --region us-west-2 --profile redwood-sso` now returns a token string. `kubectl get pods -n redwood-dev` still says Forbidden though.

eng-infra: final piece: your AWS Identity is probably mapped to an IAM role that needs to be bound to a k8s RBAC group. We manage that mapping via aws-auth or an OIDC mapping. I checked and your IAM principal isn't in the `redwood-dev:dev-team` k8s group. I'll submit a grant ticket to add `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-dev-sso` to the `dev-team` clusterrolebinding.

eng-infra: created grant GR-2026 for RBAC update; engineers in `dev-team` should be able to list pods after the change (cc @pri).

pri: thanks — once it's applied, try `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n redwood-dev` again.

onboard-bot: FYI — please do not paste long tokens or credentials in chat.

alex: thanks everyone — can confirm after the RBAC change `kubectl get pods -n redwood-dev` works. Appreciate the rapid help! :rocket:
